### What problem does this PR solve? Issue Number: close #47427 Problem Summary: ### What is changed and how it works? In previous implementation, partial worker will transfer full data to final worker and the final worker will copy data that belongs to it at local. However, partial worker could transfer part of full data to the final worker and it will save many memory. ### Performance TiDB Version: a3bafcdffb10(nightly) Topology: 1*tidb 3*tikv Dataset: tpch10 Sql1(high cardinality): select l_orderkey from tpch10.lineitem group by l_orderkey having sum(l_quantity) > 300; Sql2(low cardinality): select l_discount from tpch10.lineitem group by l_discount;
 Benchmark | Sql1 | Sql2 -- | -- | -- Not improved | 14.88 | 1.8 Improved | 9.46 | 1.8   | 57.30% | 0%
 Memory Usage | Sql1 -- | -- Not improved | 33.5 Improved | 21.7   | 35.20%
### Check List Tests - [x] Unit test - [ ] Integration test - [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below) - [ ] No need to test > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed. > Side effects - [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU - [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory - [ ] Breaking backward compatibility Documentation - [ ] Affects user behaviors - [ ] Contains syntax changes - [ ] Contains variable changes - [ ] Contains experimental features - [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility ### Release note Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note. ```release-note Performance of parallel hash aggregate executor increases by 57% and we decrease about 35% memory usage. ```

issue_context.title: Parallel hash aggregation needs improvement
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Many useless copy and creation can be removed in parallel hash aggregation and it may speed up the agg's efficiency and save more memory.

review_comments: Add a comment for this check

done

In extreme cases, when all keys from other maps have never appeared in this map, the length of this map will keep increasing. 
So, should we consider the memory consumption resulting from the growth of the underlying data structure of the `w.partialResultMap`?

> In extreme cases, when all keys from other maps have never appeared in this map, the length of this map will keep increasing. So, should we consider the memory consumption resulting from the growth of the underlying data structure of the `w.partialResultMap`?

For the stability of tidb, I think conservative strategy is better and I will increase the memory consumption of these maps.

> Why change this?

Suppose we get block `1` with 2000 rows and block `2` with 1000 rows. Length of groupKey will be 2000 after handling block `1`, then we receive block `2`, if directly return groupKey, the length of groupKey will be 2000, not 1000.
